text: Petrovietnam to invest VND133 trillion in Nghi Son Economic zone

Petrovietnam's investment portfolio in central Thanh Hoa province's Nghi Son Economic Zone focuses on ports and logistics, crude oil storage, petrochemicals, chemicals, and fuel distribution, with total projected capital estimated at approximately VND133 trillion (nearly $5.16 billion), paving the way for new development opportunities for the province's industrial and energy hub.
However, many projects are still in the research phase, completing procedures, and selecting investors.

At a recent conference in Hanoi, the People's Committee of Thanh Hoa Province and the Vietnam National Oil and Gas Group (Petrovietnam) reviewed the implementation of their cooperation agreement and agreed on tasks to promote investment projects in the area.
The focus is on enhancing coordination, addressing delays, and turning cooperation orientations into specific projects.
In Thanh Hoa, 12 units within Petrovietnam's ecosystem operate in fields such as petrochemicals, technical services, construction, fuel trading, fertilizers, banking, and insurance.
In the first 10 months of 2026, these units achieved a total revenue of VND251.3 trillion, contributing VND22.48 trillion to the state budget.
The Nghi Son Refinery and Petrochemical Plant operated at an average capacity of 121% over ten months, meeting about 40% of domestic fuel demand.
Petrovietnam's contribution is also evident in employment and social welfare.
The group's units provide jobs for nearly 2,500 workers in the area.
From 2020 to 2025, Petrovietnam and its member units supported Thanh Hoa with VND 334 billion, including funding for the construction of 96 Great Solidarity houses, 17 schools, and 13 hospitals.
This foundation allows both parties to expand cooperation, with the Nghi Son Economic Zone being a key area.

Over the next five years, Petrovietnam plans to allocate approximately VND 133 trillion for investment in Nghi Son, including ports and logistics; crude oil storage; petrochemicals and chemicals; and fuel distribution.
This portfolio aims to develop links around the Nghi Son Refinery and Petrochemical Plant, better exploit existing infrastructure, and expand supporting industrial activities.
The national crude oil reserve and commercial storage project is identified as a top priority by the province.

Previously, at the Thanh Hoa Investment Promotion Conference 2026, the Prime Minister and a working delegation surveyed the proposed site for a storage facility with a capacity of about 1 million tons, covering an area of 60 hectares in Hai Binh Ward.
The establishment of the reserve is set within the requirement to enhance energy security and support raw materials for petrochemical activities.

In addition to the oil storage, the exchange portfolio between the two parties includes 11 post-refinery chemical projects, such as sulfuric acid production, ammonia solution, carbon black, hydrogen recovery, and hydrogen peroxide production.
Seaport, inland port, oil and gas services, and logistics projects are also under consideration.
The VND133-trillion investment is the projected scale for these project groups; not all projects have been approved or have investment decisions.

After more than nine months of implementing the cooperation agreement signed in early February 2026, the crude oil storage in Nghi Son has been included in the planning and identified as a national priority investment project; the post-refinery chemical portfolio has expanded to 11 projects.
The Nghi Son Integrated Oil and Gas Services Port project is nearing the completion of investment policy adjustment procedures.
However, some tasks remain slow, including determining the scale and land needs of certain projects, selecting investors for chemical projects, and finalizing land clearance costs.
These are stages that directly affect the investment preparation progress, site allocation, and the ability to synchronously implement components in the area.

At the conference, Chairman of the provincial People's Committee To Anh Dung requested Petrovietnam to promptly survey to agree on the oil storage boundary, coordinate to propose necessary mechanisms to the Central Government, and work with the Nghi Son Refinery and Petrochemical Plant on the possibility of sharing crude oil reception infrastructure.

The province commits to updating planning, proactively clearing land when project boundaries are available, assigning leaders to monitor each project, and shortening the time to handle procedures within its authority.

For chemical projects, the province requested Petrovietnam to coordinate to promote Nghi Son Refinery and Petrochemical Plant and capital contributors to quickly select investors, prioritizing projects that are ready and financially capable enterprises.
Both parties also agreed to maintain a coordination mechanism, regularly review progress.
The progress of resolving bottlenecks and the extent to which the proposed portfolio is transformed into projects eligible for implementation will be an important measure of the cooperation program.

In the distribution sector, Thanh Hoa supports PVOIL in expanding the Nghi Son warehouse, cooperating with Petrolimex, and developing a fuel retail network, while requiring adherence to principles of equality, transparency, and respect for business autonomy.
The province also proposed researching investment in infrastructure for Industrial Zone No. 6 and Zone A in sync with the crude oil storage project.
These contents will need to be specified through planning, investment procedures, and implementation plans of each investor.
